chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who became junub (in a state of major ritual impurity) during the night of Ramadan, then deliberately omitted the ghusl (ritual bath) until dawn broke. He said: He must free a slave, or fast two consecutive months, or feed sixty poor people. He said: And he said: It is fitting that I do not think he will ever attain it.

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: Became junub (state of major ritual impurity)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for deliberately delaying ghusl until dawn in Ramadan?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes the major expiation (kaffarah al-kubra) for deliberately missing the Fajr prayer and breaking the fast by remaining junub until dawn, emphasizing the severity of the negligence. The three options—freeing a slave, fasting two consecutive months, or feeding sixty poor people—mirror the expiation for accidental killing, highlighting the gravity of the sin. The Imam’s remark that it is 'fitting' he will not attain the reward underscores the principle that deliberate omission of obligatory acts without valid excuse forfeits their spiritual merit.
